title: CUDA kernel optimization notes — FlashAttention, fused ops, paged KV (v3)
content:
Context:
These are working notes for CUDA-level optimizations we're exploring for the serving runtime: integration of FlashAttention where appropriate, broader fused-op strategies (qkv, attention+softmax, cache-aware fused kernels), and a paged KV cache design that trades device DRAM for host-backed capacity for long-context workloads. This doc collects assumptions, microbenchmarks we've run, open questions, and next steps.

Goals:
- Reduce end-to-end p99 latency for short-context requests (<= 128 tokens) by optimizing attention kernel path.
- Improve throughput (tokens/sec) for mixed batch sizes using fusion and reduced kernel launches.
- Enable models with large effective context by introducing a paged KV cache with predictable latency degradation and eviction policies.
- Keep integration surface minimal so Hosted/Dedicated/Private ABI differences are small.

High-level notes / assumptions:
- Target GPUs: A100 40GB and H100 (primary), also need to keep Ampere 80GB/RTX for dev.
- Models: Llama-family derivatives and some decoder-only T5-style models. Architectures are causal-decoder with rotary/rope.
- We assume kv cache layout is (batch, n_heads, seq_len, head_dim) in contiguous device memory when resident.
- Network I/O and RPC overhead dominate for very small token counts; kernel optimizations only help where compute != trivial.

FlashAttention integration:
- FlashAttention v2 provides fused attention with lower memory footprint by streaming and recomputing some intermediates. Good for long sequences and memory-limited cases.
- Pros: large reduction in workspace; often faster for long seq_len (>512) and high head_dim (>=64).
- Cons: For small seq_len (<=128) and small batch sizes, overhead of the more complex kernel can make it slower than optimized cuBLAS+custom softmax. Also FlashAttention API requires specific tensor layouts and supports a limited set of masking patterns.
- Actionable integration plan:
  - Implement runtime-level kernel selector: if seq_len >= 256 OR (head_dim >= 64 AND seq_len >= 128) -> prefer FlashAttention; else prefer micro-optimized fused kernels we maintain. Selector must be tunable via config and model profile.
  - Add a microbenchmark harness in tests/bench/flash_selector that runs representative cases and logs which path is chosen.
  - Keep a shim that converts our internal KV layout to FlashAttention expected layout without extra copies where possible (prefer views).

Fused ops strategy:
- Targets for fusion:
  1) q,k,v linear projection + reshape + transpose -> fuse into single kernel producing packed QKV buffer to avoid 3 separate GEMMs when possible (or at least fuse post-gemm transposes).
  2) attention: integrate fused scaling + masked softmax + dropout + multiply with V into one kernel where memory allows.
  3) MLP: fused linear1 + activation (GELU/SiLU) + linear2 + bias-add where head_dim fits into L2 to reduce round trips.
- Implementation notes:
  - For QKV: still rely on cuBLAS for the heavy GEMM when batch*seq*embed is large; but fuse the subsequent reorder/back-to-back kernels. For small sizes implement a custom small-GEMM path (cutlass-based).
  - Keep fallbacks for fp16/ampere+TensorFloat modes; fused kernels must support fp16/bf16 and optionally int8/quantized kernels later.

Paged KV cache design (draft):
- Motivation: Support application-level long contexts (e.g., retrieval-augmented generation, chat history) without requiring full context resident on device for every request.
- Basic idea: Keep a hot working set of KV shards on device; cold shards are paged to host or remote storage. Shards are contiguous ranges of sequence positions (or chunked per N tokens).
- Key components:
  1) Pager: async IO engine that moves pages host<->device. For private deployments this can use pinned memory + RDMA if available.
  2) Eviction policy: LRU-ish with awareness of request patterns (prefers keeping recent utterances + high-reuse retrieval docs). Allow pinning for explicitly referenced contexts.
  3) Cache indexing: global sequence IDs map to (page_id, offset). We store a compact metadata table on device for quick lookups.
  4) Consistency: for streaming generation we must guarantee that current step uses the correct KV state. Pager can supply future pages speculatively for beam/parallel generation.
- Latency model:
  - Device-hit: baseline kernel latency (no page transfer).
  - Host-hit (page-in): additional page transfer cost (PCIe / NVLINK / RDMA). Need to quantify typical 8KB–64KB page sizes.
  - Recommendation: default page size = 64KB (configurable). Small pages increase lookup overhead; large pages increase transfer cost.
- Integration with scheduler/batching:
  - Scheduler must be page-aware. We should avoid co-scheduling requests that cause competing page-ins to oversubscribe PCIe.
  - Prefer grouping requests by context affinity to maximize device residency reuse.

Benchmarks we ran (summary) — microbenchmark harness on A100-40GB, batch sizes [1,4,8,16], seq_len [32,64,128,256,512], head_dim=64:
- Baseline (cuBLAS + custom softmax):
  - batch=1, seq=64: 8.3 ms p50 attention kernel, p99 ~ 12.1 ms
  - batch=8, seq=128: 22.0 ms p50, p99 ~ 28.5 ms
- FlashAttention (v2):
  - batch=1, seq=64: 9.7 ms p50 (slower for small seq)
  - batch=1, seq=512: 35.0 ms p50 (significantly faster than baseline ~48.0 ms)
- Fused fused-attention (our prototype):
  - batch=1, seq=64: 6.8 ms p50 (best for small seq)
  - batch=8, seq=128: 17.5 ms p50
- Observations:
  - FlashAttention shines for long sequences (>256). Our fused small-seq kernels win for production short-context workloads.
  - Kernel launch overhead and memory allocs dominate at batch=1; batching improvements matter.

Open implementation questions / risks:
- Numeric divergence: FlashAttention uses recomputation and different reduction orders; we need to validate that output distributions are acceptably close for our eval sets (QA/chat). Create automated regression tests.
- Masking patterns: FlashAttention supports causal masks; we need to ensure its mask API covers our multi-hop attention masks used in some models (sparse / block-sparsity).
- Maintenance burden: keeping two attention codepaths increases complexity. Need good tests + simple selector config.
- Paging correctness during failure/rollback: ensure partially-paged-in states do not produce inconsistent output; add strong invariants in the pager.
- Multi-tenant interference: on dedicated GPU nodes, different tenants may cause thrashing of pager. Scheduler should consider tenant-level isolation.

Experiment plan (next 6 weeks):
- Week 1–2: Extend microbench harness to include more head_dim values (32/64/128) and dynamic shapes; gather heatmaps and generate selector rules. Owner: Marcus Li.
- Week 2–3: Implement FlashAttention shim (zero-copy views where possible) + kernel selector flag (config). Owner: Dani Rodriguez.
- Week 3–4: Implement basic pager prototype (host-backed pinned memory) with simple LRU. Start with synchronous copy path for correctness. Owner: Aisha Patel.
- Week 4–5: Run regression evals on QA/chat eval set (2000 prompts) to detect quality drift between paths. Owner: Ethan Moore.
- Week 5–6: Integrate pager with scheduler; test multi-request scenarios and measure end-to-end p99 changes. Owner: eng-serving-runtime team.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Add SRV-1234 test vectors to microbench harness (Marcus).
- [ ] Create PR with FlashAttention shim + selector (Dani) — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- [ ] Pager MVP: host-pinned copy path + simple LRU + metrics (Aisha).
- [ ] Define default selector thresholds and expose via model_profile.yaml (team).
- [ ] Perf dashboards for these experiments (observability) — include trace ids, kernel timings, PCIe metrics.

Notes / scratch ideas:
- Consider prefetching pages based on retrieval ranking scores — e.g., if RAG returns top-k docs, prefetch those pages while tokenization runs.
- Use compressed KV pages (fp16 delta encoding) to reduce transfer sizes for host-backed pages; decompress on device in a kernel.
- For fused QKV, explore Cutlass fused GEMM kernels for small-M and small-N cases; may beat cuBLAS for small seq.

References / links:
- FlashAttention v2 repo + paper (internal link): https://github.com/HazyResearch/flash-attention
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- JIRA: SRV-1234 (paged KV design)
- Confluence design notes: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=87321

Questions for the team (to resolve in design review):
1) Thresholds: where should the default threshold between FlashAttention and fused kernels live? Per-model profile or global runtime config?
2) Page size: 64KB default okay? Need math on average tokens/page with our tokenization.
3) Pager auth model for Private deployments: do we allow customer-managed RDMA or always mediated by control plane?

If you see anything missing or have additional microbench cases to add (sparse attention, rotary vs rope), drop into SRV-1234 or ping me on Slack (@aisha).

-- Aisha
